name: libspng
workload: PNG decode throughput in the Wuffs 'mimic' benchmarks (wuffs bench -mimic): six test images from about 19 KB to 4 MB of decoded bytes, 8-bit gray/palette, 24 bpp and 32 bpp, libspng 0.7.3 versus libpng 1.6.37 as shipped with Debian Bullseye.
claimed_speedup: libspng vs libpng (MB/s, ratio taken from the page): 19k_8bpp 125 vs 122 (1.02x); 40k_24bpp 155 vs 147 (1.05x); 77k_8bpp 384 vs 370 (1.04x); 552k_32bpp verify_checksum 392 vs 289 (1.36x); 4002k_24bpp 225 vs 214 (1.05x); 552k_32bpp with checksum ignored 461 MB/s (1.60x, against libpng's verify_checksum figure because libpng's simplified API cannot skip the checksum). The project's own README says only that it 'outperforms the reference implementation in common use cases' and shows a performance chart image (libspng.org/perfx86.png) with no numbers in the text.
compiler_and_flags: Benchmark harness built per the Wuffs doc: 'gcc -O3 test/c/std/<codec>.c' plus the mimic cflags (-DWUFFS_MIMIC -lm -lpng -lz), results given for clang 11.0.1 and gcc 10.2.1; the libspng mimic code #includes spng.c into the harness (test/c/mimiclib/png.c), libpng and zlib 1.2.11 are the Debian-shipped libraries so their own build flags are not stated.
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz, Debian Bullseye, measured September 2022
tradeoffs: Smaller API than libpng and not API compatible; single spng.c/spng.h can be dropped into a project; can use miniz instead of zlib; animated PNG is only planned; focus on security (OSS-Fuzz) and ease of use. Some optimisations and test images come from libpng and carry the PNG Reference Library License v2 (see usability note).
caveats: The numbers are third-party (Wuffs author) from September 2022 on one laptop CPU and one decoder harness (full-image decode to a BGRA or 8-bit buffer; libspng outputs RGBA8 because it has no BGRA8). The gain over libpng is only 2-5 percent on five of six rows; the 1.36x and 1.60x wins are on the one 552k 32bpp image, and the 1.60x row uses a different checksum mode than the libpng baseline. The libspng README performance claim is an image only, and libspng.org was not reachable from this session to read the chart. The last commits on master (2026-08-31) are a copyright-year bump and a merge; the previous functional commit is Dec 2023 and the last release is v0.7.4 (May 2023). Encoding speed is not covered by any number found. The repo also contains libpng-derived optimisations under the PNG Reference Library License v2, a permissive licence.
